findings.title: Public findMany() removed from InsightsBookingService without a replacement for callers
findings.body: The diff deletes `findMany(findManyArgs)`, which executed the scoped query against `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized`, and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment. Any caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` will fail to compile or run after this change. The PR description says only the integration tests were updated and does not mention this removal, so the breaking change is undocumented. The PR should either keep a query-executing method or confirm that no callers remain in the repo.

findings.title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions because authConditions is always truthy
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (never null or undefined), so `authConditions` is always truthy. The `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches are therefore only reachable in the `authConditions` falsy case, which cannot happen. The code is misleading: a reader would assume the NOTHING_CONDITION fallback applies when there are no filters and no auth, but in that situation the auth fragment (`1=0`) is returned through the first branch. The logic should be simplified to make the actual behavior explicit.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted with no replacement
findings.body: The `Caching` describe block ("should cache authorization conditions" and "should cache filter conditions") is removed entirely. The service still memoizes `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, so this behavior is now untested. The PR description does not mention removing these tests. They should be restored, adjusted to the Sql format, or the removal should be justified.

findings.title: Final integration test asserts exact row set against a shared table without scoping to test data
findings.body: The `$queryRaw` test runs `SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ${baseConditions}` and expects `toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])`. The query is not restricted to the test's own data, so any other booking in the database that matches the user scope and event type (leftover data or parallel tests) makes the assertion fail. The original test used `toHaveLength(1)` against the service result. The assertion should be scoped to the created IDs or check membership instead of exact equality.

findings.title: Tests assert exact SQL fragment structure, making them brittle and weakly behavioral
findings.body: Most authorization and filter tests compare `Prisma.sql` objects with `toEqual` against full SQL template literals, including whitespace-sensitive parameter arrays and operator ordering. These tests fail on any cosmetic change to the SQL and do not verify that the conditions select the right rows. The behavioral check is limited to one test that executes the query. The PR description says the tests were copied from the routing service, but this brittle pattern should not be propagated without a database-backed check of each scope.
